content.title: About
content.content: Pepperoni is a flavorful sausage made from a blend of beef and pork, seasoned with paprika, garlic, and other spices. Thinly sliced rounds are used on pizza, sandwiches, salads, and as a snack. The product has a characteristic spicy, slightly smoky taste and a firm yet tender texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pepperoni originated in Italian‑American cuisine and is considered the U.S. version of Italian salami.
The beef‑pork blend provides a more balanced flavor and texture than pork‑only sausages.
Pepperoni slices are often brushed with olive oil before baking to enhance flavor and create a crisp edge.
The red color comes from paprika and sometimes food coloring, though natural spices can also produce a vivid hue.
Thin slices quickly crisp up in the oven, forming a crunchy crust.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The beef‑pork mixture supplies a high amount of complete protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat provides heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Pepperoni contains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc is important for immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: A modest amount of monounsaturated fats from pork and beef can support heart health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Pepperoni is typically salty; excess sodium can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: It contains more saturated fat than lean meat products, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have allergic reactions to beef or pork.

items.title: Preservatives and nitrites
items.content: Nitrites are often used to preserve color and shelf life; large amounts may be undesirable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add thin pepperoni slices to pizza before baking, use them in hot sandwiches, salads, pasta dishes, or enjoy them as a snack by pan‑frying until crisp.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep pepperoni in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. Once opened, it lasts 2‑3 weeks. For longer storage, freeze up to 3 months in a vacuum‑sealed bag.
